full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that two brothers Azimuddin and afore-said Md. Hanif were the owners of the properties under partition. They were in joint mess. Azimuddin died leaving a widow name Shabjan Bibi and a son Amjad Ali and a daughter Mater Ma. The plaintiffs are the heirs of these persons. Shabjan Bibi was only aged 20 years when Azimuddin died she then remarried Md. Hanif. Thereafter Chakla Roushanabad survey operation began and the name of Md. Hanif was alone recorded as owner of the suit properties in C. R. Khatian although Shabjan Bibi and her minor children by Azimuddin were also the owners of the same. 

 6. It appears from the judgments of both the Courts below that they refused to grant temporary injunction to the plain-tiffs as prayed for on the ground that the plaintiffs could not file any documents or papers in support of their claim of title to the suit properties. The Court below also accepted the Chakla Roushanabad Khatian recorded in the name of Md. Hanif as correct on the ground that the name of elder brother used to be recorded in such khatian and there was no reason for recording the name of the younger brother (Md. Hanif) in the Khatian, if the properties were of both the brothers. The courts below also held that the plaintiffs might be adequately compensated in the event of their success in the suit. 

 8. We find that it appears from the pleadings of the plaintiffs that they have got a good prima facie case to go into trial and as such the courts below acted illegally in turning down their prayer for temporary injunction on the aforesaid short ground. A suit can be contested on the evidence both oral and documentary or on either of the two. The court below also failed to notice a vital fact that at the time of preparation of the khatian in question the elder brother Azimuddin was dead.
